articleTitle: Collaborative Computing for Space-Air-Ground Integrated Vehicular Networks
abstract: Recently, many new applications are emerging in intelligent transportation systems. Diverse vehicular services impose different QoS requirements. It is imperative to leverage the Space-Air-Ground Integrated Network (SAGIN) to serve vehicles user, by combining the respective advantages of satellite network, air network, and ground network. Motivated by mobile edge computing, researchers propose to deploy edge servers on satellites, UAVs, and HAPs and make them edge nodes. Empowered by this, the edge nodes can perform collaboratively computation offloading for computation-intensive vehicular tasks. In such a complex and heterogeneous system, how to make the task assignment decision is a critical problem. In this paper, we propose a collaborative computing service platform and formulate the task assignment problem as a linear programming problem, which can be well addressed by existing optimization tools. The collaborative computing for space-air-ground integrated vehicular networks can guarantee vehicle user experience.

articleTitle: Hurricane Damage Detection by Classic and Hybrid Classic-Quantum Neural Networks
abstract: This article describes a deep hybrid convolutional neural network (HNN) that uses one quantum device for binary image classification. The quantum device is a Ry quantum circuit with one qubit. This HNN configuration was evaluated on a practical problem - detection of damaged buildings on pictures taken from a satellite in addition to our previous attempts on the simple MNIST, MNIST Fashion and more sophisticated CIFAR10 and CIFAR100 datasets. The performance of HNN was compared with the reference classical model and two pretrained models: VGG-15 and RESNET-50. The measured metrics (accuracy and loss) during these experiments showed some drawbacks compared with the reference model but still support our assumption about the feasibility of HNN application for multiclass classification problems.

articleTitle: Application of laser-induced acoustic method on air-underwater communication
abstract: Laser-induced acoustic (LIA) technology is a possible way of communicating from an air-based platform to the underwater target in the sea. The present paper introduces a method of LIA which works in the optical breakdown mechanism. Acoustic signals with high energy were generated in the optical breakdown mechanism of a Nd: YAG laser having pulse widths about 10 ns. A DFB-FL hydrophone was designed to receive the LIA signals for the various repeated frequency of the pulsed laser. It was found that LIA signals with repeated frequency ranging from 1 to 20Hz can be detected clearly, which demonstrated the feasibility of across air-underwater communication by using LIA technology. Simulation of LIA in a distance of 400m between laser spot on the water surface and the hydrophone was performed by the COMSOL Multiphysic software. The simulated results show the communicated ability of LIA technology in the long distance.

articleTitle: Air-Ground Integrated Federated Learning: An Experimental Implementation
abstract: With the envision of sixth generation (6G) networks technology, diverse artificial intelligence (AI) services are gradually developed from the network center to the edge, which enables unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) as a hot spot to provide auxiliary services of machine learning (ML). Due to the sensitive privacy and limited resources, traditional centralized ML may not be used directly in such networks. As a promising distributed collaborative ML, federated learning (FL) is more suitable. However, the current research on air-ground integrated federal learning (AGIFL) mostly focuses on architecture design and network simulation. In this paper, we mainly verify the feasibility of deploying FL between UAV and terrestrial users through practical platform. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the training accuracy is higher when the training nodes is close to the server, and the accuracy is improved from 69.48% to 83.52% when distance is reduced from 20 meters to 5 meters.

articleTitle: A Graph Routing Algorithm Enhancing Wireless Sensor Networks Lifetime
abstract: Industrial wireless sensor networks provide wireless communication for devices and sensors. With the limited resources and interference and changes of network conditions, reliability is particularly required in industrial environments. Based on centralized network management, graph routing, which uses redundant paths to ensure reliable transmission, has arisen. In order to enhance latency, lifetime and reliability performance metrics of network, this paper proposes a graph routing algorithm Q-learning Graph Routing Lifetime Enhanced (QGRLE). Routing graph is reconstructed periodically and latency, lifetime and reliability metrics in network are optimized dynamically. Power resources are fully utilized with the consideration of residual energy of nodes. Simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms in latency and lifetime performance.

articleTitle: Experimental Results of Federated Learning in Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Swarm
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) need to deploy machine learning (ML) models to execute complex tasks such as target tracking. For traditional centralized ML, UAVs need to transmit the raw data to the ground central server for model training. However, the transmission of raw data not only causes a large delay but also may incur sensitive information leakage. Federated learning (FL) as a distributed machine learning enables multiple UAVs to form a swarm for distributed model training. Nevertheless, most of current researches on FL of UAV swarm are based on theoretical architecture and simulations. In this paper, we focus on verifying the feasibility of deploying FL in a UAV swarm through practical experiments. Moreover, we further explore the impact of the distance change between the training node UAVs and the parameter server UAV on the training accuracy. The experimental results show that the UAV swarm can perform 15 rounds of global training in 5 minutes, with a training accuracy of 84.28%.

articleTitle: Spatio-temporal Transmission of COVID-19 Pandemic in Susceptible-exposed of Small-world Network Model
abstract: This paper proposes the Susceptible-exposed of Small-world Network Model (SSEM) by combining the Susceptible-Exposed-Infectious-Recovered (SEIR) model with the Small-world Network (SN) model. The scenarios of COVID-19 propagation in urban public transport network was set by the specific model parameters. A study area, Huicheng District, Huizhou City, Guangdong Province, China, was selected to estimate the temporal and spatial distribution characteristics of COVID-19 within 12 hours based on SSEM. The results show that, without taking protective measures, if the two infectious source were in a bus, after 12 hours, 324 bus stations, 762 infected people and 68.85km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> were covered in the study area. The results of this study will provide a reference for the future study of COVID-19 virus transmission mechanism in the small enclosed environment.

articleTitle: A Building Network Security Monitoring and Management System Based on the Internet of Things
abstract: The aim of the study is to design a network security monitoring and management system based on the Internet of Things and to realize the automate management. The system is made up of three layers which are sensor layer, transmission layer and application layer, respectively. The modular structure is adopted to develop router node which have flexible structures and strong versatility. The node connects with sensors through standard analog interface. Internet of things can monitoring network security information and transmit the data to the remote server management system reliably. Experiments show that the network security monitoring and management system is stable, safe and provides basis for the scientific management.

articleTitle: Hybrid High-Speed Power Line and Wireless Communication for 5G Network
abstract: Performance of throughput, coverage and reliability in smart grid and 5G networks can be significantly improved by exploiting high-speed power line communication (HPLC) and wireless communication (WLC) simultaneously. However, coordinated use of HPLC and WLC suffers the difference of transmission characteristics and channel variability of both media. In this paper, dynamical selection of access links and power allocation is investigated for the hybrid HPLC and WLC system, where orthogonal frequency division multiplexing is utilized in HPLC and non-orthogonal multiple access is used in WLC. Since the formulated sum rate maximization problem is non-convex, constraint relaxation and auxiliary variables are introduced to transform the original problem into a convex one. Then, a sub-optimal but efficient transmission scheduling and power allocation algorithm is proposed. Further, we design an optimal solution based on branch and bound method. Finally, numerical results are provided to validate that the designed algorithm can improve sum rate significantly compared to pure HPLC and pure WLC benchmarks.

articleTitle: Review on algorithms for integrated scheduling problem of single piece and small batch products
abstract: With the development of society and the improvement of living standards, consumers prefer personalized products more and more. This makes the production mode change from large-scale production to single piece small batch production. Because of the zero inventory characteristics of single small batch products, the typical scheduling algorithms, such as job shop and flow shop algorithms, are no longer applicable. The integrated scheduling algorithm considering both machining and assembly provides a new solution for this kind of problem. It is close to the production practice and has more practical significance. This paper sorts out and analyzes the research results in the field of integrated scheduling from three perspectives: general integrated scheduling problem, special integrated scheduling problem and other problems, points out some directions and contents of integrated scheduling optimization algorithm to be further studied, and puts forward suggestions for further research.

articleTitle: Simplified Models in Evaluating the Performance of the Non-orthogonal Slotted Aloha Protocol
abstract: In this paper, two simplified models are proposed to evaluate both effectively and accurately the performance of the Non-Orthogonal Slotted Aloha (NOSA) protocol particularly suitable for satellite communications. As the NOSA system is constructed on the basis of the Sparse Code Multiple Access (SCMA) technique in a complete random fashion, it is found that the performance of the NOSA system depends mainly on the codebook collision conditions as well as power differences among colliding packets. In this case, a fitting function is first proposed to approximate the detection performance of the SCMA system in the physical layer, based on which a simplified physical model as well as an analytical model are proposed to evaluate the performance of the NOSA system. Numerical results show that both the models could effectively and accurately approximate the performance of the NOSA system, paving the way for the NOSA system to be quickly evaluated and deployed in the practice.

articleTitle: OpenAcc Parallel Schemes for Accelerating Asteroidal Period Search
abstract: The rotational period of asteroids may provide important information about the inner structure of asteroids and reveal the formation history of our solar system. Most inversion methods of searching asteroidal periods are extremely time-consuming. Therefore, some parallel technologies, such as OpenAcc, can be used to accelerate the search process. In this article, two parallel schemes of OpenACC with CPU and GPU are presented for accelerating the period searching of asteroids from light curves. The Intel i7-9750H CPU is used to execute the CPU's serial computing and parallel computing. Furthermore, the Tesla V100-SXM3 GPU is used to execute the GPU's parallel computing. Compared with the serial scheme, the maximum speedup ratio of the CPU parallel scheme is 30.5x, while that of the GPU parallel scheme is 29.9x. The experiment results indicate that the GPU parallel scheme is more suitable for large-scale parallel computing of searching asteroidal periods. Additionally, an initial period estimation method is proposed to reduce the searching interval. It is confirmed numerically to be efficient and feasible in the application of searching four real asteroidal periods, and the derived periods are practically consistent with the results obtained by other methods.

articleTitle: Vision for Space-Air-Ground Integrated Radar Network
abstract: Confronting with new challenges including new threats, new resource constraints and new environment, one single radar, one radar platform or radar netting system will face the risk of decrease in overall detection efficiency. Hence, a novel Space-Air-Ground Integrated Radar Network (SAGIRN) is proposed in this paper based on collaborative Cloud-Edge- Terminal (CET) architecture. SAGIRN has several inherent features including All-Domain Integration, CET Collaboration, Dynamic SoS Reconfiguration, Menu-type Solution Matching, Smart Processing in Real Time and Iterative Evolution, and can efficiently integrate all kinds of battlefield radar resources to achieve global coverage, real-time response, optimal detection, flexible survivability, sense-to-decision-making in the whole battlefield or in a specific area.

articleTitle: Review of distributed integrated scheduling algorithms
abstract: The research object of integrated scheduling Institute is single piece and small batch order production. This kind of order is characterized by multiple varieties and small batch, which puts forward a severe test to the flexible production capacity of enterprises. Nowadays, with the rise of Internet of things technology, collaborative cooperation among enterprises is possible. Distributed collaborative manufacturing can effectively integrate enterprise resources, reduce the risks caused by enterprises fighting alone, improve the flexible production capacity of enterprises, and finally enable manufacturing enterprises to improve production efficiency and reduce unknown risks. However, the research on distributed integrated scheduling problem is still in its infancy, and there are few research results. This paper analyzes and studies the research status of the problem from four aspects: symmetric resource distributed integrated scheduling problem, asymmetric resource distributed integrated scheduling problem, multi-objective distributed integrated scheduling problem and special distributed integrated scheduling problem, points out some directions and contents of distributed integrated scheduling optimization algorithm to be further studied, and puts forward suggestions for further research.

articleTitle: Review on Space High Precision Time-Frequency Transfer Technology
abstract: Spatial high-precision time-frequency transfer technology will promote the application of high-precision time frequency reference. It is the core competence to establish a spatial time-frequency system. This paper describes the error of space high-precision time-frequency transfer and reviews the development of time-frequency transmission technology. The evolution of transmission carrier from microwave to laser, error processing from terminal direct measurement to system precision correction, transfer accuracy from ns level to ps level or even higher, application scenarios from single link building to constellation networking, from satellite- ground link, inter-satellite link to serving deep space are concerned, which will promote technological upgrading of ultra-high precise time-frequency transfer.

articleTitle: Dynamic Monitoring Urban Expansion of Huizhou from 2000 to 2020 Using the Google Earth Engine
abstract: Huizhou is located in the Pearl River Delta of Guangdong Province, bordering Shenzhen and Hong Kong. It is one of the rapidly developing cities in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. With the accelerating process of urbanization, the land use change of built-up areas in Huizhou is also increasing. This paper uses Google Earth engine (GEE) cloud computing platform, selects multiple periods Landsat remote sensing data, uses CART data classifier to discriminate urban land, vegetation land and water body, and implements dynamic monitoring of Huizhou urban expansion from 2000 to 2020. The results show that the urban area changes to an increasing trend from 2000 to 2020, with a total increased area of 350.13 km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Based on the extracted urban built-up area of Huizhou in 2000, 2005, 2010, 2015 and 2020, the growth rates of urban area in recent years are: 10.63% in 2000–2005, 3.84% in 2005–2010, 5.82% in 2010–2015 and 8.24%in 2015–2020, respectively. This study will provide a data basis for the analysis of urban future planning in Huizhou.

articleTitle: Plane Wave's Spatial Property in Marine Environment
abstract: Maritime atmospheric turbulence has been the-oretical investigated, since it can affect optical waves more obviously than it propagate in terrestrial turbulence. In this study, we obtain the new analytical expressions for the phase structure function of plane waves propagating in the anisotropic maritime atmospheric turbulence. Based on these expressions, the formulas of the angle-of-arrival fluctuations of optical waves are derived. The anisotropic parameter, the power law exponent, are considered in the numerical results.

articleTitle: Integration of Low Earth Orbit Satellites with Terrestrial Cloud-edge Systems
abstract: With the rapid deployment of low earth orbit (LEO) satellites, the integration of LEO satellites with terrestrial cloud-edge systems has attracted the attention from academia to provide ubiquitous services. This paper first reviews the existing terrestrial cloud-edge systems and the emerging LEO satellites in details. Furthermore, we propose the integration of orbital edge computing with terrestrial cloud-edge systems to utilize the computation and communication resources of both LEO satellites and terrestrial cloud-edge systems. To fully exploit the potential of LEO satellites, dealing with the challenges of orbital dynamics, intermittent connectivity and significantly constrained power capacities is of vital importance.

articleTitle: Computation Offloading Strategy of Multi-satellite Cooperative Tasks Based on Genetic Algorithm in Satellite Edge Computing
abstract: Satellite network has become an important supplement to the ground backbone network by the virtue of its wide coverage. Furthermore, satellite edge computing cluster can also provide real-time computing support for ground-based and space users. Focusing on the scenario where a task set consisting of multiple independent tasks which have high QoS requirements is offloaded to the satellite edge computing cluster, this paper establishes a model for transmission delay and calculation delay of computation delay, and proposes GASECO, a satellite edge computing offloading algorithm based on genetic algorithm. As shown in the simulation experiments, this algorithm improves the QoS of satellite edge computing services, shortens the response delay of task set, and reduces the failure rate of task offloading through the collaboration of satellite edge nodes.

articleTitle: Efficient Edge Intelligence under Clustering for UAV Swarm Networks
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are expected to be widely used in many critical applications including monitoring, surveillance, urban target tracking, and delivery of goods, from military to civil fields. To realize that, empowering UAV swarm with edge intelligence is becoming appealing and inevitable. Federated learning (FL) as an emerging distributed collaborative machine learning (ML) without letting raw data out, could be suitable for UAV swarm networks but remains largely unexplored. In this paper, we first investigate the problem of efficient Edge Intelligence under Clustering for UAV swarm networks (e-EIC), i.e., how to jointly optimize the computation resource allocation and UAV clustering to minimize the total energy consumption of the UAV swarm for FL, subject to the training accuracy and latency constraints. We decompose the challenging e-EIC problem into two subproblems: computation resource allocation and UAV clustering, and accordingly propose an iterative algorithm based on the optimal policy of the first subproblem and local-search techniques for the second subproblem. Extensive performance evaluations demonstrate that our proposed algorithm can reduce more energy consumption of UAVs than three baseline algorithms, while satisfying the training accuracy and latency constraints.

articleTitle: A Satellite Network Data Transmission Algorithm Based on Adaptive LT Code
abstract: As an effective supplement to terrestrial communications, satellite communications play an important role in global communications. However, in satellite communication networks, communication resources are limited, data transmission links are unstable, and satellite communication has signal attenuation and transmission delay. How to enable stable and efficient data transmission is a major challenge in satellite communication networks. Data coding plays an important role in satellite communication since it avoids the need of frequent feedbacks in the transmission process, ensures reliable communication, and reduces receiving delays. In a practical satellite network, when the transmission channel condition is unstable, using fixed encoding packet size may lead to prolonged delay and reduce the effective data transmission rate. Therefore, it is particularly important to adaptively adjust the size of encoded packets according to the file size and network environment. In this paper, we propose a satellite network data transmission algorithm based on adaptive fountain codes. The data is transmitted in LT codes. We propose two algorithms, including a two-side-search dynamic iterative algorithm and adaptive packet size encoding transmission algorithm to find the optimal encoding packet size and grouping to minimize the total delay and improve the effective data transmission rate. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm has a smaller delay and a higher effective data transmission rate than those using the fixed packet size algorithm. When the bit error rate is high, it can also maintain a low delay and a high effective data transmission rate.

articleTitle: WSpeed: Drone Energy Optimization for Multiple-Package Delivery Considering Weight Changes
abstract: Drones are increasingly used in daily or urgent package delivery with their outstanding flexibility and rapid response capability, especially in scenarios like post-disaster relief, medical supply dispatch, etc. However, due to the limitations of drone battery size and load capacity, the delivery coverage scope and the number of packages can be delivered per time are highly constrained. In addition, the delivery order of packages also affects the quality of service due to the different urgency levels of packages. Since the flight energy dominates the total UAV energy consumption, it would be very beneficial to find energy-saving methods for the package delivery scenarios, through more energy-efficient drone speed and trajectory scheduling. In this paper, we propose WSpeed, an energy optimization algorithm that jointly considers the drone speed and flight path optimization with urgency differences of delivery points, for the multiple-package delivery scenarios. WSpeed is based on a novel drone energy consumption model, which provides a key finding, that as the total drone weight changes, the drone energy consumption per unit distance, as well as the most energy-efficient speed also changes. Therefore, during a multi-package delivery flight, the UAV speed should be adjusted adaptively to achieve the best energy efficiency. Moreover, WSpeed clusters delivery points based on the load capacity and the distance between points, for more efficient path scheduling. Besides, WSpeed also considers the different package urgency priorities during the delivery, which is closer to the real-life scenarios. Experiments show that WSpeed can save as much as 27.2% energy and 36.5% cumulative flight time over existed approaches while achieving the minimum service utility.

Index Terms: Speed Of The Unmanned Aerial Vehicles

articleTitle: New Crowd Sensing Computing in Space-Air-Ground Integrated Networks
abstract: With the development of Space-Air-Ground Inte-grated Networks (SAGINs), how to design a distributed task cooperation mechanism with low-latency computing, high data rates, low delay and high coverage is an important research content. Crowd Sensing computing could provide the effective solutions for SAGINs. This paper first considers the combination of SAGINs with crowd sensing computing for improving the task completion efficiency in SAGINs. The crowdsoucing methods are considered into the SAGINs in order to solve the complex and large-scale sensing tasks. In this paper, based on Blockchain and Multi-access Edge Computing (MEC), the traditional centralized application service architecture is transferred into a lightweight and distributed network architecture. Under this lightweight and distributed network architecture, this paper proposes a Q-learning based Task Cooperation (QTC) mechanism through dividing the three-dimensional space based on Voronoi diagram. We conduct the comparison experiments for the proposed QTC mechanism on real dataset. The performances of the proposed QTC mechanism on rate of task completion and total income of task execution are evaluated by the comparison experiments.

articleTitle: A Dependency-Aware Offloading Algorithm based on Deep Reinforcement Learning for Vehicular Networks
abstract: Recent years have witnessed the explosive growth of ubiquitous vehicles with extremely intelligent systems, which results in large amounts of data generated. Most of these vehicle applications have the characteristics of computation-intensive and latency-sensitive. Especially, with the rapid development of communication technology, the Internet of Vehicles (IoV) faces formidable challenges imposed by resource-constrained devices and the requirements for low time delay and energy consumption. To address this issue, regarded as a promising solution, Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) can enable vehicles to offload tasks to edge servers for processing. Computation offloading is a critical technology that decides which tasks should be offloaded for minimizing the total cost. However, conventional methods are inefficient to deal with multi-user vehicular networks. Since fine-grained task scheduling can reduce processing latency and power consumption significantly, in this paper, we employ Directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) to describe application and further design a distributed computing offloading algorithm. To be specific, the task offloading decision is illustrated as a Markov decision process (MDP), meanwhile an optimized deep reinforcement learning (DRL) method based on partition-based prioritized experience replay (PPER) is put forward to improve training efficiency of the network. Moreover, in order to extract deeper features of the state, this paper optimizes the actor and critic networks. Numerical results verify that, compared with the existing offloading methods, the proposed algorithm performs more efficiently on delay and energy consumption.

articleTitle: Collaborative Control and Optimization of QoS in 5G and Industrial SDN Heterogeneous Networks for Smart Factory
abstract: The 5th generation mobile communication system (5G) and industrial Software Defined Network (SDN) heterogeneous network architecture is the main networking method for the production management network of smart factories in the future. High data rate, low latency and mobility are the characteristics of those production management applications accessed by 5G. This paper analyzes the problems of QoS guarantee in heterogeneous networks of 5G and industrial SDN, and proposes a QoS collaborative control architecture for heterogeneous networks. The new architecture introduces the Flow QoS-coordinator functional entity, and defines the QoS collaborative control process among the entity, application systems,5G and industrial SDN networks. This paper introduces the network slicing capability in industrial SDN network, and constructs a traffic flow path network model. Considering the sensitivity of data transmission delay in industrial production management applications, the SDN flow path planning and global dynamic optimization method based on the dual parameters of communication rate and transmission delay are given. The scheme improves the real-time performance of flow path planning for new access services, and ensures the QoS of these existing services. Establishing QoS flows dynamically for application services avoids reserving too much bandwidth for these highly mobile and high-speed services, which can reduce the cost of network construction.

articleTitle: Olive Branch Learning: A Novel Federated Learning Framework for Space-Air-Ground Integrated Network
abstract: Space-air-ground integrated network (SAGIN) can provide global data collection to support various data-driven artificial intelligence (AI) services, especially in some remote areas where terrestrial communication facilities are unavailable (e.g., desert and isolated islands). However, the hierarchical data collection mode of SAGIN faces the challenges of redundant data collection, ineffective data transmission and privacy concerns. To this end, we first propose a novel configurable federated learning approach in SAGIN environment, namely Olive Branch Learning (OBL). Specifically, it consists of a ring structure LEO constellation in the space layer, and two-tier star structures imposed on the air nodes and IoRT devices in the air layer and the ground layer, respectively. Then, an efficient clustering and mapping algorithm is designed for OBL by taking into account the model bias of the air nodes as well as their geographic distributions. The objective is to minimize the time cost required to train the global model to achieve the preset accuracy. Extensive experimental results based on realistic learning datasets demonstrate the superior performance of our algorithm over the benchmark policies.

articleTitle: E-Cube: Energy-efficient UAV Trajectory Scheduling with Height and Speed Optimization
abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are increasingly used in data collection from IoT ground nodes (GNs) in different wild areas and scenarios, such as visiting GNs on electrical transmission towers along the mountains, or flood monitoring GNs on the banks along the rivers. However, limited battery capacity greatly restricts the performance of UAV in above applications. In this paper, we propose E-Cube, a UAV energy optimization scheme that jointly considers speed and height scheduling. E-Cube first decomposes the UAV spatial motion in terrain with altitude fluctuation into the horizontal plane and the vertical plane for energy efficient solutions. On the horizontal plane, E-Cube performs a Speed-Sensitive Trajectory Selection Algorithm (STSA), which is based on a practical energy model, to schedule the speed and select the distance accumulation trajectory. For the method on the vertical plane, an Altitude-Sensitive Trajectory Selection Algorithm (ATSA) is adapted to select the trajectory with the minimum height changes greedily based on the local information and then optimizes energy consumption for flight control by reducing speed varying based on the global information. E-Cube is evaluated through a series of experiments, and the results demonstrate that E-Cube can save as much as 25.1% energy consumption on average compared to existed approaches.

articleTitle: On Dynamic Routing Technology for Space Network
abstract: Since the topology of space network is time-varying, dynamic routing is a key technology to realize networked space system. In this paper, a typical link state routing protocol, i.e. OSPFv3, is chosen as the dynamic routing protocol for space networks and two improvements have been adopted to alleviate the high protocol overhead and slow routing convergence problem of OSPFv3 when directly applied to space network. Firstly, we analyze the characteristic of space links and conclude that point-to-point network type can reduce protocol overhead. Secondly, we introduce the decoding lock flag of the links to the detection process of link state change to quicken the routing convergence process. Then, the improvements for OSPFv3 protocol are implemented on a space router and the architecture of the space router is introduced. Finally, we conduct three tests to evaluate the performance of the implemented OSPFv3 protocol. The performance evaluation results show that the implemented OSPFv3 protocol is compatible with terrestrial COTS router. The response delay of local link state change is about 192 ms. The onboard route computation overhead is less than 17 ms in a 5 node network on a 64 MHz SPARC processor.

articleTitle: WinCross: Find the Energy-efficient Crossing Window for UAV with Joint Optimization of Path and Speed
abstract: Data collection from a series of IoT ground nodes is a common scenario for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) applications in the wireless sensor network area in recent years. However, a key limitation lies in the energy efficiency of UAV due to the very limited battery capacity in contrast to the long service time demands. Thus, it's highly desired to reduce the energy consumption of UAV by optimizing its path and speed without affecting the completion of data collection tasks under the transmission time requirements. In this paper, we propose WinCross, a novel algorithm that jointly optimizes the path and speed of UAV with minimized energy consumption. WinCross can first derive an energy-efficient crossing window that the UAV should pass through, during the trajectory scheduling. It utilizes a proposed original projection method that can map a 3D problem (GN location and transmission ranges on the 2D plane, plus the minimum transmission time on the temporal dimension) to a 2D problem, that can reduce the optimization complexity remarkably. Secondly, WinCross can further optimize the energy consumption by classifying all feasible crossing window cases and scheduling the corresponding trajectory and velocity respectively. Based on an iterative approach, WinCross can complete all transmission tasks while minimizing the energy consumption. Experiments demonstrate that WinCross can save as much as 22.2% energy over baseline.

articleTitle: Cooperative Task Processing for the Internet of Remote Things through Ultra-Dense Satellite Systems
abstract: Recent advance in ultra-dense satellite communications provide an alternative solution for coverage extension and backhaul connections of the Internet of Remote Things (IoRT). IoRT devices can offload their tasks to satellite networks for processing, or relay them to the ground data center through satellite communications. However, due to the resource-constraint nature, a single satellite cannot support computation-intensive and complex execution. Therefore, this paper design a cooperative task processing scheme in which multiple satellites can cooperate in a satellite group and simultaneously process the IoRT tasks to improve the computational efficiency and resource utilization of satellite networks. The optimization problem is formulated as a Winner Determination Problem (WDP) with the objective of maximizing the completion delay reduction of all IoRT devices, and a cooperative greedy computing algorithm with a low complexity is proposed as our solution. Numerical studies show that the proposed scheme outperforms benchmark schemes.

articleTitle: Cloud-Edge Collaborative Intelligent Inference Based on Distributed Neural Networks in Power Distribution Networks
abstract: As power distribution networks (PDNs) develop, the amount of data and calculation generated by edge devices increases dramatically, bringing challenges of data storage, cloud computing and transmission bandwidth. Edge computing can be deployed in PDNs to improve the stability of energy flow and the reliability of control. In this paper, a distributed inference framework based on distributed neural networks and joint inference of edge devices and cloud devices is proposed for cloud-edge collaborative intelligent inference in PDNs. The proposed framework is formed into a joint optimization problem of error rate and inference delay, which decides whether to process inference tasks at edge or in cloud based on their difficulty. Value Decomposition Network (VDN) method is adopted to optimize computation offloading decisions. Simulation results demonstrate that the performance of VDN method is the best among five methods. VDN method can adapt to changes in the environment, as indicated by the fact that system offloading rate of VDN method adjusts to the changes.

articleTitle: Multi-State Energy Efficiency Improvement Strategy for DRX Functional Devices
abstract: Ensuring the high efficiency of communication is one of the important properties of the Internet of Things (IoT) device network, which can be realized by Discontinuous Reception (DRX). In this paper, a strategy is proposed to schedule the user equipment (UE) with the base station knowing whether the packet is coming in the following 1 or 3 time slots, and this mechanism is added to an IoT device model with DRX function. This model operates on 5G standards and communicates with base stations. Packets are generated with a fixed length and a Poisson process. Based on this assumption, according to the cross-layer analysis model, this paper analyzes 1) the steady-state probability of each state, 2) the energy efficiency of this model, and 3) the improvement of energy efficiency relative to that of the single-mode circuit. It can be observed from the theoretical and simulation results that this model can improve the energy efficiency on the basis of the original strategy.

articleTitle: Efficient Single-Group Multicast Beamforming: A Determinantal Point Process Approach
abstract: The problem of single-group multicast beamforming (SMBF) is well-known NP-hard. It motivates the pursuit of computationally efficient near-optimal solutions. Due to multicasting, the multicast group is bottlenecked by the user(s) with the minimum received signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). This paper proposes to solve the SMBF problem in two steps: i) select the bottlenecking users by a machine learning approach based on determinantal point process (DPP); and ii) design the beamformer for the selected users. The DPP model jointly considers the magnitudes and directions of users' channel vectors, and thus enables an efficient selection of the bottlenecking users. The beamformer is specifically designed for the selected users by applying the QR algorithm, which facilitates the computation by leveraging channel orthogonalization. Numerical results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed algorithm in terms of the performance-complexity compromise.

articleTitle: Mixed Strategy PSO for Global Optimization
abstract: Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) is an evolutionary algorithm for solving global optimization problems. In recent two decades, a lot of researches have been working on improving the performance of PSO and numerous PSO variants have been presented. According to a recent theory, the hardest problem to one evolutionary algorithm may be the easiest to another algorithm, and vice versa. Thus, mixed strategy PSO algorithms might be more efficient than pure strategy algorithms. A mixed strategy PSO algorithm (MSPSO) was proposed which integrates five different PSO variants. In MSPSO, an adaptive selection strategy is used to adjust the probability of selecting different variants according to the rate of the fitness value change between offspring generated by each variant and the personal best position of particles to guide the selection probabilities of variants. The rate of the fitness value change is a more effective indicator of good strategies than the number of previous successes and failures of each variant. The proposed algorithm is tested on CEC 2014 benchmark suites with 10 variables. Experimental results demonstrate that the solution accuracy of the proposed algorithm is overall better than those of comparative algorithms.
